newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SUPERB JUVENTUS READY TO CLAIM WORLD CROWN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUPERB JUVENTUS READY TO CLAIM WORLD CROWN.

text.p: Juventus head for Tokyo and their World Club cup match with River Plate of Argentina next Tuesday poised to be crowned as the best club side in the world.
On the evidence of their performance in beating Manchester United 1-0 at Old Trafford on Wednesday night, few could realistically argue the European champions will not do just that.

On a night of intense passion, emotion and sheer noise, generated by an expectant 53,000 flag-waving home crowd, Juventus gave a dazzling first-half display of movement, passing and athleticism which left United trailing to a 35th minute Alessandro Del Piero penalty at the break.

In the second half they weathered almost constant United pressure, soaking up attack after attack, riding their luck at times but also playing classic defensive football, to pull off a famous win in a memorable match in which the losers were far from disgraced.

Juventus, who beat Manchester United 1-0 in Turin in September have now become the second side to win a European tie at Old Trafford in three weeks -- a ground where United had not previously lost in 40 years.

Coach Marcello Lippi, who has re-built his side in the six months since they won the European Cup in May, was delighted afterwards, praising his men -- particularly goalscorer Del Piero -- for the way they performed, but congratulating United too.

"That was a very, very tough match for us to win, United played some outstanding football, especially in the first half, but I am pleased and proud that Juventus have become the first Italian side to win a European club match here.
"Now we have a long trip to Tokyo and for a moment we can forget the Italian League and the European Cup.

"We are only two points behind Inter in the league and Inter have to play Milan while we are away, so we can relax slightly, let them battle each other, and look forward to another good match in Tokyo."

The only goal came when Del Piero lashed home a penalty after he had been upended by Nicky Butt just inside the penalty area. At the time United were reeling, having had to re-organise their team after only 12 minutes when defender Phil Neville limped off with a hamstring injury.
But even allowing for that, Juventus deserved to be leading at the interval.

Frenchman Zinedine Zidane who has lost weight and gained in confidence since his summer move from Bordeaux to Juventus, controlled the midfield and together with compatriot Didier Deschamps, Vladimir Jugovic, the tireless Alen Boksic and the scampering Angelo Di Livio, kept United chasing black-and-white striped shirts all over the pitch.

If United were given a football lesson when they lost to Juventus in Turin, and handed more of the same in the first half, they at least showed all their fighting qualities in the second, illustrating how they won two English cup and league doubles in three seasons.

It was their turn to dominate after the interval and although they never quite matched Juventus's imperious patterns, they created more chances against the Italians than most sides have done all season.
United manager Alex Ferguson said afterwards he was unhappy to have lost, but delighted to have been part of such an outstanding game.

"Juventus were fantastic and they proved tonight, especially in the first half why they are European champions. Their work ethic was superb, every player earns his money, they have experience and threats in all the right places. It was no disgrace to lose to them."

The outcome means Juventus, who last lost to an English club in Europe 17 seasons ago, have won Group C and will now play either arch-rivals Milan, or possibly Norwegians Rosenborg in the quarter-finals.
But while Manchester United have slipped to third in the group behind Fenerbahce, who beat them 1-0 at Old Trafford three weeks ago, they are not yet out.

If they avoid defeat in their last match at Rapid Vienna in two weeks time and if Juventus beat Fenerbahce, United will finish second in the group and face Group D winners Porto in the quarter-finals next March.
